subject: Intermittent connectivity to Acme private deployment - escalation
messages:
From: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: networkops@acmecorp.com
Date: 2026-03-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intermittent connection failures to private deployment - Acme Prod VPC

Hi Marissa / Dev,

We started seeing intermittent failures to our Redwood private deployment in the Acme Prod VPC starting late Friday. Symptoms:
- 502/504 errors in our service logs when calling the API (timeouts during TLS handshake).
- Packet captures show repeated RSTs and occasional ICMP unreachable messages.
- Traceroutes look inconsistent — sometimes traffic takes a different transit path.

This is impacting a small subset of critical traffic (about 2% of requests) but in production so high priority. We are using AWS Transit Gateway connecting to our on-prem firewall via an IPsec VPN. On-prem team reports the firewall NATs egress and has MTU set to 1500, but internal devs have enabled jumbo frames on the internal LAN (9000).

Can someone from Redwood look into routing/NAT/MTU issues on your side? We have attached a short pcap and a traceroute output. We can open a maintenance window in the next 48 hours.

Attached: acme_pcap_03012026.pcap (pcap), traceroute_acme_03012026.txt

Thanks,
Sara Jensen
Network Ops Lead
Acme Corp

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent connection failures to private deployment - Acme Prod VPC

Thanks Sara — looping in infra (Vivek) and my manager (Rishi).

Quick ask to help us triage:
1) Can you also provide a routing table export from the on-prem firewall/gateway and the exact Transit Gateway route table entries for the Acme VPC?
2) Please confirm whether the VPN is over AWS Managed VPN or a third-party appliance and whether BGP is enabled.
3) If possible, run a short tcpdump on the on-prem egress showing the TLS handshake + IP/ICMP messages (5–10 seconds during an occurrence).

Initial hypothesis: MTU mismatch / PMTU blackhole or asymmetric routing due to NAT and multiple egress devices. We will check security group / NACL rules and ensure ICMP type 3 code 4 (fragmentation-needed) is not being dropped.

If you can share the additional files I’ll do a deep-dive and propose a remediation plan.

—Dev
Dev Patel
SRE, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

From: networkops@acmecorp.com
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent connection failures to private deployment - Acme Prod VPC

Dev — attaching the extra outputs you requested.

Files attached: routing_table_acme_03012026.txt, traceroute_acme_03012026.txt, acme_pcap_03012026.pcap

Notes from on-prem:
- VPN: third-party appliance (FortiGate 7.2), with active/standby pair; BGP is enabled.
- Transit Gateway has route propagation enabled; main route points to the VPN attachment.
- On-prem NAT translates source to a pool of public IPs for egress.
- MTU on the firewall external interface is 1500, internal interface shows 9000 on the LAN side (for storage traffic).

We captured a small pcap during a failed request. The pcap shows TLS ClientHello and then many ICMP "fragmentation needed" (type 3 code 4) messages and then the session resets. Traceroute occasionally shows an extra hop through a partner peer.

Thanks — we are ready to coordinate a maintenance window if you need config changes on our end.

—Acme Network Ops

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@acmecorp.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent connection failures to private deployment - Acme Prod VPC

Thanks for the captures — I dug into the pcap and traceroute. Summary of findings: 
- I see repeated ICMP type 3 code 4 (fragmentation needed) messages coming from an intermediate hop. The MSS values in the TCP handshake point to a lowered path MTU (~1360).
- After the ICMP messages, TLS ClientHello sometimes triggers a reset. This is classic PMTU discovery failing due to ICMP being dropped or NAT interfering with ICMP replies.
- Security groups on the Acme VPC side appear to allow the ephemeral return ports; NACLs are permissive. I don't see blocked return traffic on our VPC side.
- There is evidence of asymmetric return path — I can see SYN from client -> our endpoint via path A, but the reset/ICMP comes back via path B (different peering), likely due to your active/standby VPN pair and partner peering.

Proposed immediate mitigation (low-risk, short maintenance window):
1) Temporarily allow ICMP type 3 code 4 on the on-prem firewall (if currently blocked) to enable PMTU discovery end-to-end.
2) As a quick workaround, reduce the MTU on the on-prem external interface (or set TCP MSS clamping) to 1420 to avoid fragmentation across the VPN-transit chain.
3) Add a static route on the on-prem firewall for the Redwood endpoint prefix(s) pointing explicitly to the primary VPN device to avoid asymmetric egress for those flows.

If the above is accepted, I can provide CLI commands for FortiGate and a rollback plan. Longer-term: we should coordinate with the partner peer to ensure consistent MTU and avoid asymmetric routing, or add stateful inspection exceptions for fragmentation-needed messages across NAT.

Attaching: proposed-fix-commands.txt

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@acmecorp.com>, networkops@acmecorp.com
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Escalation: Private connectivity — proposed actions & maintenance window

Sara / Acme team,

Thanks — we agree with Vivek's findings and propose the following coordinated plan:
- Window: 2026-03-03 01:00–02:00 UTC (we can shift on request).
- Steps (owners):
  1) Acme: apply TCP MSS clamp to 1420 on the on-prem egress or reduce MTU on external interface (Acme network ops) — (rollback: restore MTU to 1500).
  2) Acme: permit ICMP type 3 code 4 for PMTU discovery across the VPN for the Redwood endpoint prefix (Acme network ops).
  3) Redwood (Vivek): will monitor for packet drops and TCP handshake success from our side; will provide logs and pcap capture during window.
  4) Redwood (Dev): prepare temporary route pinning instructions and config snippets for on-prem (if Acme agrees).
- Success criteria: error rate for calls to Redwood <0.1% over 30 minutes post-change.
- Escalation contacts: Rishi Malhotra (rishi_malhotra@redwood.com), Vivek Kulkarni (vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com), Sara Jensen (sara.jensen@acmecorp.com).

Please confirm the window or propose an alternate. I opened a ticket: JIRA SUP-8792 and put a shared doc with runbook and rollback steps in the Drive link above.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@acmecorp.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, networkops@acmecorp.com
Date: 2026-03-03T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: Private connectivity — proposed actions & maintenance window

Rishi / team —

We ran the maintenance at the proposed window. Actions taken:
- Applied TCP MSS clamp to 1420 on the FortiGate on-prem egress.
- Confirmed ICMP type 3 code 4 is allowed over the VPN for the Redwood endpoint prefixes.
- Added a static route for Redwood prefix to force primary VPN peer for return traffic.

Initial results: traffic stabilized during the 30-minute post-change period. Error rate dropped to near zero in our synthetic tests. We'll monitor for 48 hours and report any regressions.

Thanks for the clear runbook and quick turnaround. Can we schedule a 30-minute post-mortem next week to talk about long-term fixes (partner peering, MTU harmonization)?

—Sara
Sara Jensen
Network Ops Lead
Acme Corp
